title: Two orchestras breathe the same melody
question: How do Stokowski and Monteux make room for the opening melody’s long phrases?
intro: Stokowski recorded the Philadelphia Orchestra on 12 November 1934; Monteux’s San Francisco recording dates from 3–4 March 1942. The comparison uses Stokowski’s first disc side against the corresponding opening of Monteux’s complete movement. The accepted window stops before the side’s later material; no whole-movement speed claim is made.
